decision.format: BF16 K/V on full-attention layers 3,7,11,15,19,23; Hadamard-group32 INT8 K/V with FP16 scales on layers 27,31,35,39
decision.gguf_native_fidelity: accepted for the full 11-prompt 512/8 and 4K/16 gates plus bounded mixed_v1 128K/16 transfer
decision.paro_native_fidelity: rejected: one prompt fails at 512/8 and two prompts fail at 4K/16
decision.physical_256ki: blocked: the quality-preserving BF16 prefill oracle runs out of memory on the RX 7900 XTX request-scratch probe
decision.summary: Keep the implementation as an explicit diagnostic only. GGUF fidelity transfers and its matched eager p512/d128 speed is flat within noise, but PARO fidelity does not transfer and its graph decode is 4.11% slower. The quality-preserving 256 Ki PARO path OOMs cleanly; the only allocation-passing direct-streaming control is already correctness-rejected.

gguf_graph_capture_smoke_p512_d128.claim: graph admission and no-regression smoke only; not a speedup claim

protocol.capacity: Physical RX 7900 XTX request-scratch allocation for 262,144 prompt tokens plus 128 decode tokens, max_sequence_length=262,400, auto-tuned 768-row low-memory chunks.
limitations: The source tree was dirty during measurement, so no throughput number is retained as a repository topline.
The 128K quality transfer is one bounded mixed_v1 case, not the full 11-prompt suite.
The 256 Ki probe allocates production request scratch but does not run full prefill/decode after allocation.
The physical 256 Ki probe is PARO only; GGUF's larger resident weight footprint is not claimed to fit 256 Ki.
The direct packed-attention prefill route is allocation-only evidence because its native 512/8 fidelity is rejected.
protocol.performance: Physical RX 7900 XTX, c1 repeated token 9707, 512 prompt tokens, 8 decode warmups, 128 measured decode tokens. PARO uses three separate graph runs per layout. GGUF eager uses one persistent session, one warmup run, and three measured resets per layout. The GGUF graph rows are one-sample capture smokes only.
protocol.quality: Native BF16 reference and mixed-layout candidate sessions. Candidate decode is teacher-forced with BF16 reference tokens. Every prompt independently requires mean KL <= 0.05 and top-1 agreement >= 90%. The layout audit requires six BF16 and four packed INT8 full-attention layers, FP16 group32 scales, and no persistent BF16 shadow or surviving prefill oracle.

provenance.source_state_note: The native acceptance and performance runs used the exact implementation working tree later committed with this artifact. Because the source was not a clean committed revision during measurement, every speed row is diagnostic and performance_claim remains false.
